sources.title: Assessing Community Vulnerability to Landslide and Flood in Northwestern Rwanda
sources.organization: International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction; UCLouvain repository
sources.temporal_coverage: Household survey conducted May-July 2023; article published 2025.
sources.methodology: Repository abstract reports a 904-household survey across 50 cells and principal component analysis.
sources.limitations: Only the repository abstract was inspected; its linked full-text PDF returned HTTP 502, and the abstract does not name the higher-risk cells.

sources.title: Climate vulnerability in Rwanda
sources.temporal_coverage: District assessment published in 2026; the publisher page describes change over the previous five years without specifying those years.
sources.methodology: Publisher summary describes mixed quantitative and qualitative research on district climate vulnerability and grassroots policy implementation.
sources.limitations: The publisher page's detailed summary was inspected, but its linked full report download failed; the summary omits the sample design and index formula.

sources.title: Rwanda NDC Deep Dive: Advancing Financial Innovation to Scale up Climate Action (P172153), Implementation Completion and Results Report
sources.temporal_coverage: Implementation and results of the NDC Deep Dive project through 2024.
sources.methodology: World Bank completion report reviews the project's outputs, implementation, outcome indicators, and lessons.
sources.limitations: Project-specific results do not establish national adaptation effects; the report notes that the weather-information system's use and effectiveness could not be verified.

sources.title: Rwanda Emergency Connectivity Restoration Project (RECOR): Environmental and Social Management Framework (Draft)
sources.temporal_coverage: Draft project framework dated December 2024; includes May 2023 disaster impacts and planned reconstruction measures.
sources.methodology: Draft project environmental and social management framework with national and project-area baseline information and planned risk-management measures.
sources.limitations: Draft and project-specific; some subproject locations were not identified. Its border-conflict statement is contextual, not causal analysis.

sources.title: World Bank Steps Up Support to Increase Rwanda's Resilience to Natural Disasters
sources.methodology: World Bank announcement of approved disaster-risk financing and its intended policy pillars.
sources.limitations: The announcement describes approved support and intended systems, not completed activities or measured household outcomes.

claims.locator: Repository abstract, paragraphs 1-2, survey design and vulnerability components.
claims.paraphrase: A 904-household survey across 50 northwestern cells found vulnerability varied across landslide, flood, and combined-hazard settings; location and living conditions, demographic traits, education and economic status, household structure, and prior disaster experience were contributing dimensions.
claims.limitations: The abstract does not name sampled cells or report district-level results.

claims.locator: Repository abstract, paragraph 2, Contextualized Vulnerability Index results.
claims.paraphrase: The contextualized index identified 25 higher-vulnerability cells, mainly in landslide-prone areas and concentrated in the western study area; the authors call for localized, hazard-specific mitigation.
geographies: Western part of the study area
claims.limitations: The abstract does not identify individual higher-risk cells or provide their index values.

claims.locator: Repository abstract, paragraph 2, vulnerability component results.
claims.paraphrase: Land and property ownership reduced vulnerability in the study's component analysis, while the other four identified components were associated with increased vulnerability.
claims.limitations: The abstract reports an association within the index, not a causal or household-level effect estimate.

claims.locator: Publisher page, 'Climate vulnerability in Rwanda' summary, paragraph reporting the Huye and Gisagara index values.
claims.paraphrase: Tearfund reports that Huye's vulnerability index declined to 0.556 over the previous five years as adaptive capacity strengthened, while Gisagara's index rose to 0.626.
claims.limitations: The summary does not specify the five-year period or index construction.

claims.locator: Publisher page, 'Climate vulnerability in Rwanda' summary, paragraph on smallholder adoption barriers.
claims.paraphrase: Smallholder farmers were willing to adopt agroforestry and terracing, but limited training, quality inputs, and finance impeded uptake.
claims.limitations: The publisher summary does not disaggregate adoption barriers by district or group.

claims.locator: Publisher page, 'Climate vulnerability in Rwanda' summary, paragraph on policy implementation findings.
claims.paraphrase: The review found national climate strategies relevant to local communities and associated with positive changes, but identified coordination and targeted-support gaps affecting the most vulnerable communities.
claims.limitations: The publisher summary gives no counterfactual or district-specific measure of implementation effects.

claims.locator: Publisher page, 'Climate vulnerability in Rwanda' summary, locally led restoration program description.
claims.paraphrase: Tearfund described capacity-building for locally led restoration, especially with women, to strengthen community participation in environmental decisions and local monitoring and management skills.
claims.limitations: The summary describes an ongoing program and intended capacity, not measured resilience outcomes.

claims.locator: PDF pp.12-13 (printed pp.8-9), paragraph 12, Volcanoes Region flagship project.
claims.paraphrase: The completion report describes the Volcanoes Region districts of Burera, Nyabihu, Rubavu, and Musanze, home to over 1.4 million people, as highly climate-vulnerable; floods and droughts are associated with landslides, erosion, crop losses, and infrastructure damage.
claims.limitations: This is a project-area characterization, not a comparative national vulnerability ranking.

claims.locator: PDF p.19 (printed p.14), paragraph 29, Community Adaptation Fund pilot results.
claims.paraphrase: The 2022-2023 Gicumbi Community Adaptation Fund pilot supported 2,324 people, including 47.7 percent women, in 25 cooperatives with training and funding; 192 more people in 64 cooperatives received business-planning training.
claims.limitations: Reported reach and training are project outputs, not evidence of reduced climate impacts.

claims.locator: PDF p.17 (printed p.13), paragraphs 25-26, crop insurance information system.
claims.paraphrase: A crop-insurance and weather-information database was piloted in a few locations, but the completion report's author could not verify its use, effectiveness, pilot count, or scaling timeline.
geographies: A few locations in Rwanda; locations not specified
claims.limitations: The report explicitly could not evaluate system use or effectiveness because the relevant ministry was not interviewed.

claims.paraphrase: The draft framework states that increased seasonal variability and longer-term climate change may exacerbate poverty and food insecurity and the potential for internal displacement and conflict along Rwanda's eastern and southern borders.
claims.scenario: The passage specifies no modeled scenario; it refers to increased seasonal variability and longer-term climate change.
affected_groups: people facing poverty or food insecurity
claims.limitations: This is a broad contextual risk statement in a draft project framework, not a measured or causal conflict analysis.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The ESMF states that increased seasonal variability and longer-term climate change may exacerbate poverty and food insecurity and the potential for internal displacement and border conflict.

claims.locator: PDF p.2 (printed p.i), Executive Summary; PDF p.5 (printed p.iv), prioritized districts.
claims.paraphrase: The framework cites 74 percent of district roads as landslide-exposed and lists flood- and landslide-damaged road and bridge sites in 20 districts across all four provinces after the May 2023 rains.
claims.limitations: The 74 percent figure is cited from national transport policy; the framework gives no district-specific exposure rates.

claims.locator: World Bank press release, paragraphs beginning 'The World Bank Board' and 'The $141 million operation'.
claims.paraphrase: In September 2025 the World Bank approved a $141 million disaster-risk financing operation organized around risk information and coordination, built-environment resilience, and natural-resource management.
claims.limitations: Board approval and intended policy pillars do not establish completed activities or household-level results.

search_audit.query: Rwanda climate change subnational district flood landslide vulnerability official report pdf
search_audit.outcome: Found original household research for northwestern cells, a 2026 district assessment for Huye and Gisagara, and a project ESMF naming 20 districts with damaged roads and bridges.

search_audit.query: Rwanda climate security conflict land water resource climate change research report
search_audit.outcome: No Rwanda-specific causal research was located; the draft RECOR ESMF contains a broad, conditional statement linking climate variability, poverty and food insecurity with potential displacement and border conflict.

search_audit.query: site:worldbank.org Rwanda conflict insecurity displacement climate adaptation implementation climate change environment
search_audit.outcome: No source was located showing conflict, insecurity, or displacement constraining Rwanda climate adaptation or resilience delivery; the ESMF passage identified was climate-to-FCV risk only.

search_audit.query: Rwanda climate resilience adaptation community project evaluation districts report World Bank UNDP
search_audit.outcome: Found evaluated project outputs for community adaptation and climate information in Gicumbi, district-level local restoration findings, and an approved national disaster-risk financing operation; outcomes remain project-specific or prospective.

gaps: No Rwanda-specific source found in the targeted search established an observed climate-to-FCV pathway; the only explicit country-specific link identified was a broad potential-risk sentence in a draft project ESMF.
The reverse-FCV search did not locate evidence that conflict, insecurity, or displacement has constrained Rwanda's climate adaptation or resilience delivery.
The UCLouvain full-text PDF and Tearfund full report could not be retrieved; their claims rely on accessible publisher abstracts and summaries.
The UCLouvain abstract does not identify the individual higher-risk cells, limiting finer subnational mapping.
Most resilience evidence covers plans, project outputs, or a pilot rather than independently measured reductions in climate vulnerability.
